# Bullet lists and vertical rails

Model: `list-rail`. Each call creates a complete slide. Inter, geometry and text sizes are fixed.

[Model index](../../../templates/MODELS.md) · [Palette and content guide](../../STUDIO-MODELS.md)

```latex
\studiosetup{palette=light}
\studiotemplate[variant=three-items]{list-rail}
```

Simple three-, four- and five-item lists support light and blue; blue is the dark treatment. Specialized variants keep their native palette.
Unsupported explicit choices fail. A global palette leaves special compositions in their native treatment.

## Variants and named fields

[Complete usage reference: counts, palettes, defaults and wrapping](../../STUDIO-LISTS.md)

The number of items is selected explicitly by `variant`; it is not inferred from filled fields.

### three-items

Supported semantic palettes: blue, light.

| --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | <code>Title</code> | 17.0% wide × 14.7% high |
| `item-one` | <code>Supporting explanation</code> | 30.6% wide × 5.0% high |
| `item-two` | <code>Label 3</code> | 15.5% wide × 5.6% high |
| `item-three` | <code>Label 4</code> | 23.8% wide × 4.8% high |

Omitted fields retain these descriptive defaults; empty values retain their allocated space. Numbers and charts are illustrative.

Omitted fields retain these descriptive defaults; empty values retain their allocated space. Numbers and charts are illustrative.

## Complete one-slide example

```latex
\documentclass[aspectratio=169]{beamer}
\usetheme{bitpolito-studio}
\usepackage{bitpolitostudiotemplates}
\usepackage[backend=biber]{biblatex}
\addbibresource{bibliography.bib}
\begin{document}
\studiotemplate[
  variant={three-items},
  palette={light},
  title={Title},
  item-one={Supporting explanation},
  item-two={Label 3},
  item-three={Label 4}
]{list-rail}
\end{document}
```
